title: Durable, or borrowed from the cycle?
intro: Eight growth descriptions — sort each by whether the growth is durable franchise compounding or hot-cycle growth the market will re-price.

cards.text: 6–7% a year, every year, from a brand people buy without thinking
Volume growth from distribution reaching towns competitors ignore
Pricing power that quietly beats inflation each year
A decade of double-digit profit growth with RoE above 15% every year
60–70% earnings growth at the center of a global capex boom
Margins at all-time highs while three funded rivals build capacity
Revenue doubling because the industry's customers are all upgrading at once
A commodity producer's record year at peak prices

debrief: The durable bucket shares one property: the growth's CAUSE persists — brands, distribution, pricing power, franchise returns — so next year resembles this year. The hot-cycle bucket's growth is real but its cause is a phase: a capex boom, a simultaneous upgrade wave, peak prices, capacity racing in. Markets price the difference — which is why the fast one can carry the lower multiple and still be the worse buy. The question is never 'how fast?' but 'what happens to the cause?'
